title: Microsoft 365 outage — held-messages phishing pretext
summary: After a November 2026 Microsoft 365 / Exchange Online disruption, attackers sent fake service-health notices claiming held messages would be deleted within 24 hours unless recipients clicked Restore Messages. Real incident identifiers such as EX1550543 were cited to increase credibility.

keyFacts.claim: Incident identifier EX1550543 was associated with a real Exchange Online disruption.
Lures claimed held messages would be deleted within 24 hours.
Primary call-to-action was a Restore Messages button or link.
Messages impersonated Microsoft 365 service-health / outage notifications.

suggestedPretexts.pretextHint: Fake service-health notice urging Restore Messages before held mail is deleted.
Fake escalation asking helpdesk to mass-restore mailboxes via an external tool.

verifyOfficiallyDefault: Check the Microsoft 365 admin center or the internal IT status page. Never use a restore link from an unexpected email.

title: nginx2root — illustrative web-server advisory
summary: Illustrative vendor-style advisory for a critical privilege-escalation issue in nginx (synthetic CVE CVE-2026-NGX2R). Affected versions 1.24.x–1.26.x on Linux. Attackers may send fake urgent mitigation or patch downloads citing the advisory.

keyFacts.claim: Synthetic CVE identifier CVE-2026-NGX2R describes privilege escalation to root via malformed request handling.
Affected product versions include nginx 1.24.x through 1.26.x.
Vendor guidance emphasizes applying the official mitigation through internal patch management.
Urgency framing: unauthenticated remote path to elevated privileges on exposed reverse proxies.

suggestedPretexts.pretextHint: Fake vendor notice urging immediate mitigation download citing CVE-2026-NGX2R.

verifyOfficiallyDefault: Open the vendor advisory from a bookmarked URL and apply patches through the internal patch-management process. Do not download mitigations from email links.

title: php2shell — illustrative web-application advisory
summary: Illustrative advisory for a remote code execution pattern in PHP application stacks (synthetic CVE CVE-2026-PHP2S). Fake hotfix or failed security-scan messages may urge operators to download a package or script.

keyFacts.claim: Synthetic CVE identifier CVE-2026-PHP2S covers remote code execution via crafted request bodies.
Affected stacks include common PHP hosting runtimes on shared and dedicated hosts.
Attacker pretexts include fake hotfix packages and failed security-scan remediation scripts.
Official remediation is via the package source and the internal security ticket queue.

suggestedPretexts.pretextHint: Fake hotfix or failed security scan urging a package/script download.

verifyOfficiallyDefault: Use the official package source and the internal security team's ticket queue to confirm any fix. Do not run scripts attached to unexpected scan alerts.

title: Java4Shell — OpenJDK Base64 memory-corruption RCE
summary: Java4Shell (CVE-2026-114938) is a critical memory-corruption vulnerability in OpenJDK's Base64 decoder. A remote attacker can overwrite heap memory and reach RCE. Pre-auth impact demonstrated on products such as Keycloak, Jira, Confluence, Jenkins, and Artifactory. Fake urgent JDK upgrade or scanner-remediation lures may target Java platform and application teams.

keyFacts.claim: CVE-2026-114938 is a critical memory-corruption bug in OpenJDK's Base64 decoder (CVSS 9.2).
Malformed Base64 (for example 64 A characters followed by =) can overwrite neighboring heap memory.
Pre-auth RCE demonstrated on Keycloak, Jira, Confluence, Artifactory, Jenkins, and PingFederate.
Official remediation is to apply vendor/OpenJDK fixed builds through internal patch management.

suggestedPretexts.pretextHint: Fake urgent OpenJDK / Java4Shell mitigation download citing CVE-2026-114938.
Fake scanner alert urging an immediate Java runtime hotfix for Jira/Jenkins-style stacks.

verifyOfficiallyDefault: Confirm Java4Shell guidance from the official advisory (calif.io/java4shell) and apply OpenJDK / vendor fixed builds through internal patch management. Do not download JDK bundles from unexpected email links.

title: Ruby2Shell — Ruby encoding upcase heap overflow
summary: Ruby2Shell is a one-byte heap overflow in Ruby's single-byte encoding case-conversion path (upcase / related APIs), present since Ruby 2.4.0. Rails and classic Sinatra are exposed by default on affected Rubies. Fixed releases include 3.3.14, 3.4.13, and 4.0.10. Self-hosted stacks bundling affected Rubies (for example GitLab, GHES, Mastodon) may see fake urgent Ruby upgrade lures.

keyFacts.claim: Ruby2Shell is a one-byte heap overflow reached via upcase / case-folding on certain single-byte encodings (sharp-s path).
Fixed Ruby releases include 3.3.14, 3.4.13, and 4.0.10; 3.2 and older remain EOL/affected.
Rails and classic-style Sinatra are affected by default on vulnerable Ruby versions.
Popular self-hosted products bundling affected Rubies include GitLab 19.6.0, GHES 3.22.5, and Mastodon 4.7.5.

suggestedPretexts.pretextHint: Fake Rails/Ruby security bulletin urging an emergency runtime upgrade package download.
Fake vendor notice for self-hosted GitLab/GHES Ruby2Shell emergency patch.

verifyOfficiallyDefault: Confirm Ruby2Shell guidance from the official advisory (verialabs.com/ruby2shell) and upgrade Ruby or vendor bundles through internal change control. Do not run upgrade scripts from unexpected messages.
